machines.name: C64 (breadbin)
machines.note: Original brown C64 (boards 326298, 250407, 250425). Chips are socketed on many boards.

machines.name: C64C (slim)
machines.note: Later C64C / 64C (boards 250466, 250469). Fewer chips; KERNAL+BASIC in one ROM; the PLA is often the 252715 or the SuperPLA on short boards.

machines.name: SX-64
machines.note: Portable C64 with built-in screen and 1541 drive.

machines.name: C64 Ultimate (2025)
machines.note: Commodore's new FPGA-based C64. No original chips to fail — most faults are settings, cables, USB devices or firmware.

safety.text: The original C64 power supply (the sealed 'brick') is known to fail with too high a 5 V output as it ages — that can destroy the RAM, ROMs, PLA and CPU in one go. Measure it before use (5 V DC should read 4.9–5.25 V) or use a modern replacement or an over-voltage protector.
Power off and unplug before opening the case or touching chips. Use an anti-static strap; pull chips straight with a chip puller and note their orientation.

symptoms.title: No power — the power LED stays off

causes.title: Power supply failed
causes.why: Old bricks fail completely or lose one of the two outputs.
checks: Measure 5 V DC and 9 V AC on the power plug pins (with a multimeter, PSU unplugged from the C64)
Try a known-good or modern power supply

causes.title: Blown fuse
causes.why: The C64 has a fuse on the 9 V AC line (and the PSU may have one inside).
checks: Check the fuse near the power socket for continuity
If it blew, look for the reason before replacing it

causes.title: Worn power switch or socket
causes.why: Breadbin power switches wear out and stop making contact.
checks: Wiggle the switch while powered; measure across it
Inspect the DIN socket pins

symptoms.title: Black screen (power LED on, no border, no text)

causes.title: Power supply out of spec
causes.why: A low or high 5 V stops the machine from starting — and a high one damages chips.
checks: Measure 5 V DC under load (e.g. at the user port pins 2 and 1)
Should be 4.9–5.25 V

causes.title: PLA chip (906114-01) failed
causes.why: The PLA is the most common failure in C64s and gives a black screen.
checks: Swap in a known-good PLA or a modern replacement
A Dead Test cartridge won't run if the PLA is dead

causes.title: RAM chip failed
causes.why: One bad RAM chip stops the C64 from booting.
checks: Run a Dead Test cartridge — the screen flashes tell you which RAM chip
Feel for a RAM chip that runs much hotter than the others

causes.title: KERNAL / BASIC ROM failed
causes.why: Without a working KERNAL the C64 never reaches the READY prompt.
checks: Try a known-good ROM or a ROM replacement adapter

causes.title: CPU (6510 / 8500) failed
causes.why: A dead CPU shows the same black screen.
checks: Swap with a known-good CPU if socketed

causes.title: VIC-II or clock circuit
causes.why: No video timing means no picture at all.
checks: Check for a picture on a different video output / cable first
Swap the VIC-II if socketed

symptoms.title: Border color shows but no READY / no text

causes.title: BASIC or KERNAL ROM
causes.why: The screen is set up but the start-up message never prints.
checks: Try known-good ROMs

causes.title: RAM chip
causes.why: Faulty RAM can stop BASIC from starting.
checks: Run a Dead Test cartridge

causes.title: Cartridge left in / dirty expansion port
causes.why: A cartridge or shorted pin can take over the start-up.
checks: Remove all cartridges and devices, clean the expansion port contacts

symptoms.title: Garbled or wrong characters on screen

causes.title: Character ROM (901225-01)
causes.why: Letters in the right places but the wrong shapes point to the character ROM.
checks: Swap the character ROM if socketed

causes.title: RAM chip
causes.why: Random characters or shifting garbage often means a bad RAM chip.
checks: Run a Dead Test cartridge

causes.title: PLA chip
causes.why: A failing PLA can mix up memory and characters.
checks: Try a known-good or replacement PLA

causes.title: VIC-II
causes.why: Rarely, the video chip itself.
checks: Swap the VIC-II if socketed

causes.title: Cable / TV audio input
causes.why: Most 'no sound' reports are the cable or the TV's audio input.
checks: Try another A/V cable and TV input
RF output carries sound too — try it

causes.title: SID chip (6581 / 8580) failed
causes.why: SIDs are sensitive and fail fairly often.
checks: Swap with a known-good SID or a modern replacement
Make sure a 6581 is in a 12 V board and an 8580 in a 9 V board

causes.title: SID supply regulator
causes.why: The 12 V (or 9 V) SID supply regulator can fail.
checks: Measure the SID's VDD pin (28)

causes.title: Keyboard contacts or connector
causes.why: Dirty contacts or a loose ribbon cable are the usual reason.
checks: Reseat the keyboard connector
Clean the key contacts (isopropyl alcohol)

causes.title: CIA chip (6526, U1)
causes.why: U1 reads the keyboard — if a whole row/column fails it is often the CIA.
checks: Run the Diag 586220 test with its keyboard harness
Swap the CIA if socketed

causes.title: The joystick itself
causes.why: Old joysticks wear out — test with another one first.
checks: Try another joystick in both ports
Most games use port 2

causes.title: CIA chip (6526, U1)
causes.why: Both joystick ports are read by CIA U1 (static or hot-plugging can kill it).
checks: Diag cartridge with joystick loopback
Swap the CIA

symptoms.title: Random crashes / freezes after warming up

causes.title: Power supply drifting
causes.why: An ageing supply can sag or climb when warm.
checks: Measure 5 V DC after 20 minutes of use

causes.title: Heat-sensitive RAM or PLA
causes.why: Marginal chips fail once warm.
checks: Dead Test cartridge left running
Carefully cool one chip at a time (freeze spray) while it runs

causes.title: Dirty sockets / connectors
causes.why: Oxidised sockets make intermittent contact.
checks: Reseat socketed chips
Clean the expansion and user ports

symptoms.title: Picture problems (no color, rolling, interference, sparkles)

causes.title: Cable / video output
causes.why: RF output is noisy; composite or S-Video (Luma/Chroma) is much better.
checks: Try an S-Video or composite cable
Check the TV supports PAL or NTSC to match the machine

causes.title: Color clock (no color)
causes.why: No color at all can be the color clock circuit or PAL/NTSC mismatch.
checks: Try another TV/monitor
Check the 8701 clock chip on later boards

causes.title: VIC-II or RF modulator
causes.why: Sparkles in some games are a known VIC-II issue on some revisions.
checks: Try another VIC-II if socketed

symptoms.title: Disk drive won't load (FILE NOT FOUND, read errors, head knocking)

causes.title: Dirty read/write head
causes.why: Decades of dust and oxide on the head cause read errors.
checks: Clean the head with isopropyl alcohol on a cotton swab

causes.title: Head alignment
causes.why: Head-knocking copy protection knocks drives out of alignment.
checks: Run an alignment test program
Re-align or have it serviced

causes.title: Disk itself / spindle speed
causes.why: Old disks fail; the motor speed can drift.
checks: Try a known-good disk
Check drive speed (300 rpm) with a speed test

causes.title: Skip the drive: SD-card storage
causes.why: SD2IEC, Pi1541 or an Ultimate cartridge load disk images instead of floppies.

symptoms.title: Disk drive has no power / no lights

causes.title: Fuse or power supply
causes.why: The 1541 has an internal supply and fuse; the 1541-II uses an external brick.
checks: Check the fuse
Measure the external supply (1541-II)

causes.title: Cable, port or TV input
causes.why: Most HDMI problems are the cable, the TV's input selection or its resolution support.
checks: Try another HDMI cable and TV input
Try another display

causes.title: Video mode setting
causes.why: A video mode the display doesn't accept gives 'no signal'.
checks: Open the Ultimate menu and reset the video settings to defaults
Use this console's remote Menu page if you can't see the menu

causes.title: Power supply
causes.why: An underpowered supply can stop the board starting properly.
checks: Use the supply that came with the C64 Ultimate

causes.title: Audio routing in the Ultimate menu
causes.why: Audio can be routed to HDMI or the analog outputs and the SID settings can mute a channel.
checks: Check the audio mixer / SID settings in the Ultimate menu
Check the TV isn't muted and the HDMI audio input is active

symptoms.title: USB keyboard, mouse or drive not working

causes.title: Device support / firmware
causes.why: Firmware 1.1.0 added mouse support for most mice; some devices still aren't supported.
checks: Try another USB port and device
Check the firmware version (Settings → firmware notice)

causes.title: USB stick format
causes.why: Drives must use a supported filesystem (FAT32 is the safe choice).
checks: Format the stick as FAT32 on a computer and copy files again

symptoms.title: A game crashes or behaves differently than on a real C64

causes.title: Settings (cartridge, REU, drive)
causes.why: Some games need a specific drive type, an REU off/on, or no cartridge.
checks: Disable cartridges/REU and use a 1541 drive with the stock ROM
Report it in Compatibility so the console keeps a history

causes.title: Firmware bug
causes.why: Firmware updates fix compatibility issues.
checks: Check for a newer firmware (notice only — updating is a manual step)

references.title: Ray Carlsen: why the Computer Saver (PSU over-voltage)
